findings.where: 01-core-flows.md §7 step 1; workflow-graph.v1.json cond_426/cond_427/cond_448/cond_454; 03-technical-plan.md:1382 vs 01-core-flows.md §2 (planning_head → 'issue #9 — private staging'); docs/contracts/epic-planning-ref.md:526; docs/contracts/epic-staging.md §1 diagram, §3, §9, §10
findings.what: The documents disagree about where the Epic's staging starts. 01 §7, the graph and 03 create staging from the recorded target base and require that the lineage from that base to the staging head has no unaccounted commit. epic-planning-ref §12, 01 §2 and the epic-staging §1 diagram start staging from planning_head, and epic-staging §9/§10 require the planning artifacts to be in the final staging tree. epic-staging §3 resolves it 'per the delivery profile's model', but the profile has no such field. Built from the target base, the planning artifacts never reach the target. Built from planning_head, the planning commits have no integration receipts, so the graph's own lineage guard would park the Epic with receipt_missing. An implementer cannot satisfy both.

findings.where: workflow-graph.v1.json recovery rows foreign_target_movement (resume_targets = [human]) and target_moved; cond_445/cond_446; src/host/staging-driver.mjs:86-95; 01-core-flows.md §8 'Target CAS' row; 03-technical-plan.md:1583
findings.what: Any ordinary commit to the target branch during an Epic is 'not attributable'. attributable() is true only when the target moved to an ancestor of a commit this Epic recorded, and under the single-CAS design the Epic never moves the target before the final CAS. Such a commit parks foreign_target_movement, whose only resume target is human, so the only way out is cancel. The one rebuild path, target_moved → apply_staging, is effectively unreachable. 01 §8 and 03 promise an 'explicit decision after investigation', but the state machine gives that decision no step to resume into. Rebuilding staging on the new base is not an overwrite, yet it is refused. On any active repository the Epic integration path therefore cannot finish.

findings.where: resources/human-decision/human-decision-request.schema.json park_reason enum and resume_target; docs/contracts/human-decision.md §2; docs/contracts/epic-staging.md §5; graph cond_438; src/host/staging-acceptance.mjs:88-94
findings.what: The human-decision contract says a packet carries the task's park.reason, but the schema restricts park_reason to 8 categories ('alignment' … 'runtime_migration'), none of which is one of the graph's 99 park reasons. The acceptance packet that epic-staging and cond_438 route through #35 therefore cannot be schema-valid. The code writes park_reason 'acceptance_missing', which the schema's enum does not allow, and resume_target 'final_cas' as a string, which is no graph step. The acceptance_missing recovery row only permits resuming at accept_staging.

findings.where: resources/epic-staging/epic-staging.schema.json acceptance vs src/host/epic-staging.mjs:103-127 and src/host/staging-acceptance.mjs:39-56,161-180 vs graph cond_434/cond_435 and 01 §7 step 5
findings.what: The closed acceptance schema, the code and the graph disagree on the acceptance record, the only gate before the irreversible CAS. The schema has kind 'human'|'pinned_auto_policy' and included_tickets, requires target_ref, recorded_target_base and delivery_profile_digest, and forbids extra fields. The code writes kind 'human'|'auto_policy' with approver, policy_ref and tickets. findings.where: docs/contracts/delivery-profile.md §4, §6; src/host/delivery-profile.mjs:26,267-281; graph cond_435/cond_441/cond_449
findings.what: finalIntegrationPlan maps each of the direct modes merge, squash and rebase to move_target. integrate_staging then performs one CAS to the accepted staging commit, and verify_target requires target OID = that commit. findings.where: resources/epic-staging/epic-staging.schema.json:30, resources/epic-staging/epic-staging.example.json:3-4, scripts/validate-epic-staging.mjs:82 vs docs/contracts/epic-staging.md:12-15 and 01-core-flows.md §7 step 1; src/host/staging-driver.mjs:17-21
findings.what: The contract and 01 §7 say the staging ref is refs/autosk/epics/<epic_ref_key>/staging, where epic_ref_key is the domain-separated SHA-256 of {project_root_sha256, epic_id} and never a display id. But the candidate's own schema accepts any segment ([^/]+), its example uses the display id 'epic-0001', and validateStaging rejects any staging_ref that does not contain the raw `/${epic_id}/`. So a ref that follows the contract is refused by the candidate's validator, while the display-id form the contract forbids is accepted. The host driver followed the wrong form: stagingRef(epicId) builds the ref from the raw epic id with no project binding, and the tests pin 'refs/autosk/epics/e-1/staging'. This contradiction on the integration-critical ref has already misled implementation.

findings.where: 01-core-flows.md §2 (security.signer_boundary paragraph), 02-architecture.md §5; scripts/autosk-flow-doctor.mjs:42-49; src/host/doctor-checks.mjs:305-351; src/host/workflow-preflight.mjs
findings.what: The design rests the whole user-authority chain on a check that combines an unreachable endpoint with a signing identity 'reported by the daemon', and says 'no boundary' therefore stops model launch mechanically. In the code the 'daemon-reported identity' is the environment variable AUTOSK_SIGNER_SAME_PROCESS, read by the doctor script; no daemon in the series has a signer, since ADR-023 is absent. 'Unreachable' means stat() failed in the doctor's own process, not in the model's, so a declared path that does not exist counts as unreachable. Setting AUTOSK_SIGNER_SOCK=/nonexistent and AUTOSK_SIGNER_SAME_PROCESS=0 makes the check pass with no signer at all. And only tests import workflow-preflight.mjs: no launch path calls it. Package §5 discloses that for the daemon preflight but not for this check, so 'mechanically, not in words' asserts a guarantee whose mechanism is an operator-set environment variable.

findings.where: compat/autosk/patches/0028-session-bound-create.patch (daemon/extensions/pi-agent/src/index.ts autoskEnv) vs 02-architecture.md §2 'Pi-провайдеры' and §6 (resolvedPiAgent delegates to stock piAgent)
findings.what: Patch 0028 puts AUTOSK_SESSION_TOKEN, the secret that authorizes task.create_bound, into the environment of the spawned pi model process, beside AUTOSK_CWD. 02 §6 says the wrapper hands off to the stock piAgent, so every model session, including an implementer with a shell, holds a working credential for bound creates. 02 §2 says a model session gets no .autosk, CLI or decision capability. findings.where: 02-architecture.md:145-147, 04-decisions.md ADR-025 (l.230-238) and ADR-083 (l.951-957), README.md rule 16 vs resources/program-capabilities/matrix.v1.json (#38 l.1260-1285; no entry mentions custody/metadata CAS/orchestrateChildBatch/gate-result receipts) and docs/contracts/sdk-write-api.md §3-§5, §9 l.72
findings.what: The design makes ADR-025 daemon workflow custody (step-capability metadata CAS against an expected head, orchestrateChildBatch, write-once gate-result receipts) a precondition for any v1 model workflow: the preflight names `workflow.custody` and refuses every daemon without it. No `required_for_v1` matrix issue owns implementing it. A grep of matrix.v1.json for custody, metadata, orchestrat and gate-result finds nothing; #4 covers ADR-023's signed authority and #5 the ref-custody helper, but nothing covers ADR-025. ADR-083 assigns it to '#40', which is outside the pinned #3–#39 inventory. The primitives it needs are the ones the #38 typed-write contract defines (metadata update against an expected revision, capabilities scoped to project/task/operation/field set that models never hold, child enroll/park, typed transitions for trusted steps), and #38 is `planned_after_v1`, not release-blocking. The matrix says a typed primitive that v1 needs may be promoted only by an explicit user decision, a successor matrix classifying it `required_for_v1`, and a new full panel. None of those exists, and sdk-write-api.md §9 instead says primitives 'rise to release-blocking' on their own. Why it matters: the one document that says what blocks the MVP leaves out a primitive the design says nothing can run without. Implementation planned from the matrix would never schedule it, and #36 could not pass.

findings.where: docs/contracts/human-decision.md §1-§3; src/host/decision-queue.mjs:111; src/host/staging-acceptance.mjs:117-140; src/host/alignment-gates.mjs:128-150; resources/human-decision/human-decision-request.schema.json:229-238 vs 01-core-flows.md §2 ('обычная daemon connection без signature не создаёт actor=user … тот же канал обязателен для … integration acceptance') and 02 §7 alignment approval identity
findings.what: There are two authority models on the host/daemon boundary and they contradict each other. The design says only a daemon UserDecisionRecord, created after a signed user-presence challenge, makes an answer a user decision. But the required_for_v1 human-decision contract and the host modules that implement it turn an answer into an 'immutable decision record' when `response.answered_by === request.required_approver`, a string equality on caller-supplied fields. alignment-gates labels that record `authority: 'user'`, and staging-acceptance turns it into acceptance of the irreversible target move. The contract, the request schema and the modules never mention UserDecisionRecord, a signature, a record id or hash, or provenance, so there is no field in which the ADR-023 record could be bound even once it exists. Anyone building from the contracts would ship an authority path that any process knowing the approver string can satisfy. Round 5's ADR-023 disclosure covers the missing daemon primitive, not this host-side contradiction.

findings.where: src/host/workflow-preflight.mjs:27-35 (planning set; comment 'Planning touches no daemon and no provider') vs resources/workflow-graph/workflow-graph.v1.json:3572 (draft_artifact kind=agent) and 01-core-flows.md §2 / 02-architecture.md §5 ('no boundary … blocks model launch')
findings.what: The only evaluator of the signer-boundary rule leaves `security.signer_boundary` out of the planning workflow's required set, on the claim that planning runs no provider. The graph's planning chain runs model steps (draft_artifact, fix_artifact), and it is where alignment decisions, the records the boundary exists to protect, are made. So a model can be admitted to exactly the phase where user authority is exercised with no boundary check, which contradicts the rule the two load-bearing documents state.

findings.where: src/host/doctor-checks.mjs:331-335 (security.signer_boundary)

findings.where: docs/contracts/workflow-factory.md §4 ('A daemon-side writer of a scoped reason owes the same: it writes … park.origin before the reason'); resources/refusal-vocabulary/refusal-vocabulary.v1.json:734-748, 1122-1130; src/host/workflow-factory.mjs:342-354; compat/autosk/patches (0 matches for park.origin)
findings.what: epic_boundary_invalid and project_boundary_invalid are declared daemon-produced and are origin-scoped, and a scoped park with no recorded origin 'permits nothing'. The obligation for the daemon to write park.origin is not part of any named primitive: it is not in ADR-023 or ADR-025 as listed, not in REQUIRED_DAEMON_CAPABILITIES, and not in any patch. It is also not in package §5. A daemon that meets every named requirement could still park these reasons with no origin, and every such Epic would then be unresumable, leaving cancel as the only exit.

findings.where: src/host/alignment-gates.mjs:47-50, 107, 154-172, 203 vs 02-architecture.md §7 (alignment approval identity), 01-core-flows.md §2 table and §8, refusal-vocabulary.v1.json
findings.what: The only host evaluator of the four alignment gates diverges from the design. (1) Its identity hashes 5 of the 12 fields 02 §7 lists, with no domain separator, subject hash, manifest hash, user-decision record id/hash, classifier, policy disposition or protocol hash, so changing those does not make an approval stale. (2) `policyAlignment` admits a policy for `brief`, although 01 §2 forbids policy from approving Brief framing or any material product decision. (3) It emits codes that are not in the vocabulary (alignment_missing, alignment_stale, policy_scope_exceeded, material_ambiguity_unresolved) and resume targets that are not graph steps (record_<kind>_alignment, await_<kind>_alignment). The graph's reasons, such as brief_alignment_required and alignment_record_stale, are declared daemon-side, so the host code and the vocabulary name the same gate in two ways.

findings.where: src/host/staging-acceptance.mjs:19-30, 37-54, 92
findings.what: The accepted staging identity does not bind delivery_profile_digest or outstanding_debt, even though the packet shows both to the approver as required facts. The comment says 'eight facts' but ten are listed. It also does not bind the controlling anchor digest that 01 §7 puts in the authorization. So a delivery-profile change after acceptance, for example pull_request to move_target, does not make the acceptance stale. The packet's resume_target is 'final_cas', which is a fault-matrix boundary name, not a graph step (01 §8 names accept_staging and integrate_staging).

findings.where: package §4 / §5 ('17 of the 42 contracts say no link measured')
findings.what: Round 5's medium is still open as disclosure only: integration-authorization, material-decisions, platform-support and sdk-write-api still have no evaluator in src/ or in the series, and producer=none now records that honestly for integration_authorization_required. Separately, alignment-gates.mjs is a real alignment evaluator that no contract row links to, so the 'no link measured' column misses load-bearing code in the other direction too.
